thread.title: Tech Today: Where’s Zuck? Defending Salesforce’s Deal, Another Micron Target Increase - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Where’s Zuck? Defending Salesforce’s Deal, Another Micron Target Increase - Barron's
text:
People are wondering when Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg will finally speak publicly about the Cambridge Analytica scandal, which has shaved about 10% of the share price / Credit: Tiernan Ray for Barron's Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Early drop on DropBox
It’s not even trading yet, but as so often happens, the shares of DropBox ( DBX ) have got some coverage in advance of the IPO this week.
Rishi Jaluria with DA Davidson initiates the stock with a Buy rating, and a $22 price target, above the announced pricing range of $18 to $20. Jaluria thinks it has a “differentiated strategy” and a nice low rate of marketing expenses.
Where’s Zuck?
Problems continue for Facebook ( FB ) over the revelation that consulting firm Cambridge Analytica had unauthorized access to user data, what has become “Facebook’s darkest hour,” as my colleague Jon Swartz terms it .
A class-action lawsuit has been filed by one shareholder, Fan Yuan, in the District Court of Northern California claiming the company made “materially false and/or misleading” claims about Facebook’s handling of user data, as related by Gizmodo ’s Bryan Menegus.
Meantime, Hannah Kuchler with the Financial Times notes how CEO and founder Mark Zuckerberg and COO Sheryl Sandberg did not lead yesterday’s staff meeting at Facebook, and how neither executive has issued any statement on the mater. Axios ’s Mike Allen relates this morning Zuckerberg is expected to speak “in the next 24 hours."
Despite the ongoing mess, Facebook stock is rebounding this morning, up $1.73, or 1%, at $169.88. The stock has lost almost 10% of its value since Friday’s session.
Salesforce’s pricey deal
Shares of cloud computing giant Salesforce ( CRM ) are down $2.90, or 2%, at $122.22, after it announced yesterday afternoon , after market close, it will buy cloud startup MuleSoft ( MULE ) for $6.5 billion in cash and stock.
The Street has very mixed feelings about this, and the two words are “ strategic ” and “ expensive ."
Credit Suisse ’s Michael Nemeroff , who has an Outperform rating on Salesforce stock, and a $135 price target, calls the deal “highly strategic, but very expensive,” at 15.8 times projected revenue for this year at MuleSoft, by his estimate.
But that’s sort of just the tenor of the times, he writes, as "increased investments in cloud technologies could lead to an uptick in software M&A this yr,” with this being the second big deal so far after SAP AG's ( SAP ) deal to buy Callidus Software ( CALD ) for $2.24 billion, announced January 29th.
Among the most bullish on the deal, Canaccord Genuity ’s Richard Davis , who has a Buy on Salesforce and a $135 target, writes that “if the shares pull back, we will be thrilled and strongly recommending buying the dip,” referring to Salesforce stock.
"Of course, if investors think this transaction through, they should be buyers of CRM because the company’s technology stack is about to get even better."
The only dissenting voice as far as the logic of the deal is Trip Chowdhry of the boutique Global Equities Research . He thinks Mulesoft is fine, but Salesforce would have been better off buying DropBox for its “scale-out storage” in order to really correct a weakness at Salesforce relative to Amazon ( AMZN ) and other cloud operators.
MediaTek in play?
One of the new acquisition targets being floated for Broadcom ( AVGO ), following the destruction of its bid for Qualcomm ( QCOM ) last week, is MediaTek ( 2454TW ), the Taiwan-based chip firm that produces parts that compete with Qualcomm, such as the baseband modem . The Chinese-language Economic Daily has a write up by Xie Jiawen, drawing mostly from a Motley Fool post the other day by Leo Sun .
MediaTek stock today closed down roughly 2% at 336 in New Taiwan Dollars in Taipei trading. Broadcom shares are up $3.33, or 1.4%, at $243.94.
Bad news flow for Apple
Bad morning of news flow for Apple ( AAPL ). Analysts John Donovan and Steve Mullane of the boutique BlueFin Research Partners this morning report that they are cutting numbers again for the iPhone, in particular the iPhone X , after chopping their numbers back in February. The authors now predict a total of 219 million phones will be sold by Apple this calendar year, which is below the Street consensus for 224 million units, according to FactSet.
Then there’s a Washington Post article by Hayley Tsukayama that states that Apple’s planned event at a Chicago school on March 27th is part of the company’s attempt to wrestle back share in the education market, where it has been losing out to Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google unit and to Microsoft ( MSFT ).
"Near the end of 2017, Google had shipped about 60 percent of the new technology that U.S. classrooms received, according to the analysis firm FutureSource,” writes Tsukayama. "Microsoft has also seen a gain, shipping roughly 22 percent of technology to schools. Apple, meanwhile, has been slipping — with iOS making up 12.3 percent of new tech shipping to classrooms and MacOS at 4.7 percent."
Apple stock is down $1.29, or 0.7%, at $173.95.
Micron targets rise again
Another day, another price target increase for memory chip maker Micron Technology ( MU ).
BMO Capital ’s Ambrish Srivastava reiterates a Market Perform rating on the shares, but raises his price target to $63 from $43, after concluding that “consensus estimates likely do not appropriately reflect ongoing strength in DRAM pricing in F3Q.” The company is set to report fiscal Q2 tomorrow, Thursday, after the closing bell, and will also offer a forecast for Q3.
Srivastava thinks Street consensus of $7.28 billion is too low: he’s modeling $7.39 billion. He sees EPS of $2.78, versus consensus for $2.64.
Srivastava’s note echoes one yesterday from Credit Suisse ’s John Pitzer Q3’s revenue in a range of $7.5 billion to $7.7 billion.
Micron stock is up 20 cents at $61.35.
Another cheer for Lam
Shares of chip equipment maker Lam Research ( LRCX ) are up $6.08, or 2.8%, at $225.21, after the stock was re-instated at Merrill Lynch by analyst Vivek Arya with a Buy rating and a $305 price target, designating it as a “top pick” in semi names.
Of course, Arya likes how the company is the "most levered to increasing memory demand,” according to a write up provided by TheFlyontheWall .
